assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 2,000 req/s peak. A booking funnel is search-dominated: 90% of traffic is availability search and hotel detail, and only 6% is a booking attempt

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: 70% hit-rate on availability search (popular city/date pairs repeat), 80% on hotel detail. A miss goes to the read replica, never to the booking primary

assumptions.subject: pay
assumptions.statement: THE AUTHORISATION TIER IS THE BOTTLENECK AT 80%, NOT THE APP TIER. What is modelled is the payment service YOU run; the card acquirer itself is not a component, because a third-party API has no per-instance price (it is billed per transaction, e.g. 2.9% + $0.30). Its capacity of 150 auth/s is deliberately set to the CONTRACTED ACQUIRER RATE LIMIT: each instance blocks on a ~150 ms round-trip, and adding instances past the contracted ceiling buys nothing. Raising that limit is worth more than any amount of app-tier scaling

assumptions.subject: pay
assumptions.statement: At 80% utilisation the M/M/1 queueing term roughly quintuples the 150 ms acquirer round-trip to ~750 ms AT THAT HOP, which drags the booking flow to ~890 ms mean and ~4.1 s at p99 while search stays near 130 ms. That is a real prediction of this model and the single most important number in the design

assumptions.subject: app
assumptions.statement: ~650 req/s per instance. Availability search fans out across a date range and every rate plan, so it is by far the most expensive read in the system

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The primary is sized for TRANSACTION CONTENTION, not throughput: at 200 req/s it reads as ~3% busy. Room inventory needs serialisable holds - two guests must not book the last room - and the v1 analytical engine models throughput only, NOT lock contention or transaction aborts. The real booking ceiling is lower than 8,000 req/s and this model does not tell you by how much

assumptions.subject: domain
assumptions.statement: Flagged high_stakes:payments - card handling and money movement require expert review before this design goes anywhere near production. Nothing here is PCI guidance

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: The load balancer is priced at 0: an ALB's hourly + LCU charge is per load balancer, not per instance, and the engine multiplies cost by instance count. Add ~$16/month plus LCU to any total you quote

_library.summary: Search-dominated booking funnel where the rate-limited payment authorisation path, not the app tier, is the constraint.
